Marissa — quick status and attached evidence drafts.

Deliverables attached: redwood_dpf_evidence_summary.pdf, network_flow_diagram.png, soc2-type2-summary.pdf

Key points (for insertion into the customer pack):
- Legal basis: Processing occurs on customer behalf; transfers from EU to US are supported via contractual safeguards (SCCs) and technical/organizational supplementary measures. We currently implement and recommend SCCs plus documented supplementary measures for high-risk regulated workloads.

- Data minimization & retention: Customer data is only persisted when necessary for inference; model caching/KV caches are scoped and TTL'd. Default request logs retained for 90 days; audit logs retained for 365 days (configurable on Dedicated/Private).

- Encryption & key management: All data at rest is encrypted AES-256. For hosted customers, keys are managed by our cloud KMS with customer-managed keys available on Dedicated/Private. Traffic in transit uses TLS 1.3 with strict cipher suites.

- Subprocessors & onward transfers: We publish our subprocessors list and require contractual flow-downs. Any third-party hosting across regions is disclosed in the subprocessor registry and requires SOC2 coverage. Onward transfers require prior notice and documented legal basis.

- Operational evidence: Included SOC2 Type II summary, network diagram showing egress boundaries and processing regions, and a short DPF evidence summary that maps each DPF principle to technical artifacts.

I flagged one item for Laura: MedSynth asked whether Redwood participates in the EU Data Privacy Framework (DPF) certification. We do not self-certify to the DPF at this time; our standard approach is SCCs + technical measures. Please confirm the suggested legal language and any optional fallback (i.e., customer-specific commitments for Dedicated/Private deployments).

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.io
[Attachments: redwood_dpf_evidence_summary.pdf, network_flow_diagram.png, soc2-type2-summary.pdf]

Thanks — reviewed Rishi's tech notes and drafted a DPA annex matrix (attached). Highlights:

- DPF vs SCCs: Given Redwood is not DPF-certified today, recommend we state a default position: SCCs + supplementary technical measures for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private customers we can offer additional contractual commitments (e.g., KMS residency, dedicated tenancy) subject to review.

- DPA annex: I've drafted redlines and a matrix that maps each customer ask to proposed clause text. Items likely to be negotiated: data residency carve-outs, logging retention beyond default, and narrow exceptions for emergency disclosures.

- Evidence packaging: Suggest we include the SOC2 summary, the network diagram, and the DPF evidence summary. For MedSynth (regulated healthcare), call out the option for a Private deployment scoping (air-gapped or VPC) if they need stricter controls.

One open question for Sales: Do we want to proactively offer a Statement of Processing Location (SPL) for the MedSynth account to help satisfy their internal auditors? If yes, I can prepare an SPL stub to include.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
